relevance_note: Narrative review whose Tables 1-3 and Section 2 describe individual previously published patients with TNFAIP3 variants: 'Several mutations have been described in the TNFAIP3 gene, leading to A20 haploinsufficiency-related diseases'.
method_note: METHOD: Read the whole paper (narrative review; no patient labels). A Python script in my scratch directory parsed the three Markdown literature tables (Table 1: 6 rows, Table 2: 46, Table 3: 14) only to produce exact row-segment spans; every value and feature was entered by me from reading, and the script output was checked against the tables. All spans were checked verbatim against the paper, and every row was checked for all schema fields and enum values. LABELS/SCOPE: Each table row = one individual labelled 'Table n row k' (no label column). A Section 2 narrative paragraph was linked to the table row with the same variant designation (and, where two rows share a variant, the same reference number). Relatives described individually in the narrative got their own rows, labelled '<relation> of Table n row k' (25 relatives). One extra person: 'ref [34] patient' = the second Leu303fs*26 patient ('The other patient had retinal vasculitis and acneiform lesions'), who is not in Table 2. Every person comes from earlier reports; source_reference_in_review holds the printed reference. POOLED ROWS: some table rows summarise a whole family or several patients (age range, or the text says so): Table 2 rows 5 (Arg87Ter, 8 patients), 20 (Phe224Ser fs*4), 34 (Cys478Ter, two siblings), 37 (Lys564Ter), 38 (His577Alafs*95, mother and three children), 41 (Thr604Argfs*93), 44 (Glu730Ser fs*83, two patients) and 45 (Gln737Ser fs*79). The symptoms cell of row 7 (Lys91Ter) also mixes the proband and relatives. Each was kept as ONE row; its table-cell features use evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. To avoid double counting, family members inside these rows got no separate rows. Also no rows for: relatives mentioned only as unnumbered groups (other relatives [32]; daughters of the proband [73]; the patient's children [61]; affected relatives [36,37]; mother, uncle and grandmother [62]; brother and father [54]; 'one family member' [35]); and the father and mother of the Leu218Trp fs*10 patient [47], who have non-HA20 conditions and were neither tested nor called affected. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) The 119 kb microdeletion paragraph cites [25,27], but Table 1 cites [28] for the microdeletion. I linked it to Table 1 row 6 by variant designation. Its text 'no additional developmental delay was observed' conflicts with 'developmental delay' in the table; both rows were emitted. Its impaired growth and hepatosplenomegaly also resemble Table 1 row 1 [25]. (2) Table 2 row 1: 'arthritis' vs 'There were no joint issues', so the arthritis checklist item is 'not reported'. (3) Onset in the table vs the text (the table value is recorded): T2 r3 11 years vs arthritis before her first year; r9 2 years vs 3 months; r12 2 years vs first year; r16 3 years vs teenage years; r20 28-61 vs 5-10 years; r26 4 vs 5 or 6 years; r37 1.5 and 21 years vs 1 month-10 years; r38 9-41 vs before 10 years; r40 32 vs symptoms at 36; r41 28-64 vs 15; r44 1 month and 10 years vs 6 months-10 years; T3 r1 29 vs 15; r4 13 years vs 15 months; r6 4 years vs teenage years. (4) Family history: T2 r35 'Positive' vs 'None of his relatives presented with similar disease phenotypes'. T3 r2 'Positive' vs 'No other affected family members were found'. T3 r6 'De novo' vs an affected mother, grandmother, aunt and cousin; its table symptoms (fever, vomiting, abdominal and joint pain) also differ from the text (oral ulcers, nephrotic syndrome); all are recorded. (5) Citations: Pro268Leufs*19 table [49] vs text [73]; Thr604Argfs*93 table [48] vs text [49]; Section 4 cites [69] for Ala434Ter (table [30]); Section 4's 'Glu187Ter' with proliferative glomerulonephritis matches no row and was not recorded. The features of Table 2 rows 37 and 44 look swapped relative to the text (cerebral infarction is in row 44, but the text gives it under Lys564Ter); each row keeps its own cells. (6) T2 r18: the text says 'negative autoantibodies ... disappeared' but the table says 'positive autoantibodies' (the table is recorded). VARIANTS: Recorded as printed; protein strings have no 'p.' and no transcript is printed. Variant type follows the authors' wording: the Table 1 title (large deletion), the Table 3 title (missense), explicit text (splice for c.1906+1G>C, c.1906+2T>G and c.634+2T>C; nonsense for Lys91Ter; missense for Leu275Pro). Otherwise it follows the Table 2 title ('splice site, frameshift, or nonsense variants'), read with fs or Ter notation. Val309dup and the 'ref [34] patient' variant are not classed. Inheritance is never recorded: the 'de novo' mentions (Table 1 row 5, Pro226Leu fs*2, Leu303fs*26 [50], Table 3 row 6) give no parental-testing statement. Carrier parents are recorded as variant rows (father of T3 r3, mother of T3 r10), and the probands' parental_testing_statement quotes them. MEFV p.Met680Ile and p.Arg761His are attributed to 'The patients' of [73] as a group, not to a specific person, so they are left out. IL36RN c.115+6T>C is recorded for T2 r13. Zygosity is never stated per person. CONVENTIONS: Table ages without units ('10', '5', '4', '32', '29') and age ranges get no ISO value. Plain 'fever' is not mapped to the checklist's recurrent fever; recurrent, periodic, intermittent and episodic fever are. Cytopenia (autoimmune) is mapped only for immune, autoimmune or hemolytic cytopenias and for 'autoimmune-related' cytopenia (T2 r35); autoimmune hepatitis only for T2 r35 ('autoimmune-related ... hepatitis'). Unspecified 'ulcers', 'mucosal ulcers' and 'oral/genital ulcers' are not mapped. Cerebral infarction and hemorrhage are mapped to CNS involvement. 'Initially diagnosed with interstitial lung disease' (T1 r5) is mapped to ILD. n_patients_reported and cohort size are not stated. prior_report_citation is 'not reported' because each person carries their own reference in source_reference_in_review.
